instruction.text: Are the statements true or false?

atoms.a: There are many types of adverbs, and they don’t necessarily always end in “-ly”.
atoms.sound: There are many types of adverbs, and they don’t necessarily always end in L Y.

atoms.a: Adverbs also modify other words in a sentence to answer the questions how often, how, when, where and to what extent.
atoms.sound: Adverbs also modify other words in a sentence to answer the questions, how often, how, when, where, and to what extent.

atoms.a: The sentence “Amir is never late” contains an adverb.

correct.text: “Never” is an adverb that tells you how often something happens.
correct.sound: Never, is an adverb that tells you how often something happens.

instruction.text: Which part of the sentence shows how often something happens?
instruction.sound: ssml: Which part of the sentence shows how often something happens?

finish.text: Adverbs of frequency show how often something happens. They are usually placed before the main verb in a sentence.

atoms.b: Eliza ((always)) remembers the most important dates.
She would ((never)) forget a special friend’s birthday.

instruction.text: Which part of the sentence shows how something happens?
instruction.sound: ssml: Which part of the sentence shows how something happens?

finish.text: Adverbs of manner share how something happens. They are usually found after the main verb or after the object in a sentence.

atoms.b: His bow swept ((swiftly)) across the strings.

instruction.text: Which part of the sentence shows when something happens?
instruction.sound: ssml: Which part of the sentence shows when something happens?

finish.text: Adverbs of time share when or for how long something happens. They are usually placed at the end of the sentence.

atoms.b: He told me about the weekend plans ((yesterday)).
The lake sounds fabulous, I’ll let you know if I’ll be able to make it by ((tomorrow))!

instruction.text: Which part of the sentence is an adverb and shows where something is happening?
instruction.sound: ssml: Which part of the sentence is an adverb and shows where something is happening?

finish.text: Adverbs of place share where something happens. They are usually placed after the main verb or after the clause that they modify.

atoms.b: Lexy looked ((everywhere)) in the house for her power drill.
She eventually found it in the shed ((outside)).

instruction.text: Which part of the sentence is an adverb and shows to what extent or degree something happens?
instruction.sound: ssml: Which part of the sentence is an adverb and shows to what extent or degree something happens?

finish.text: Adverbs of degree share to what degree of intensity something happens. They are usually placed before an adjective, verb or another adverb.

atoms.b: Mary-Ann should have been cautious before eating the ((extremely)) hot pizza.
She burnt her mouth and now her taste buds are ((quite)) numb.
Now, she knows she won’t be ((too)) greedy with the next bite.
